_offlineAcceptanceNotes.IMAGE_DIGEST: PLACEHOLDER - replace with ECR registry digest after push; never use LOCAL_IMAGE_ID here. Decided 2026-11-18 (deploy-runbook section 1.6 item 5): the app image goes to a private ECR repository and is deployed by its registry digest; the docker save/load decision XB-10 covers the backup tool image only. Record the git SHA, the ECR tag and the digest together (runbook section 1.4)
_offlineAcceptanceNotes.CLAMAV_IMAGE_DIGEST: PLACEHOLDER - the ClamAV sidecar image pinned by its registry digest. Mirroring it into ECR is the RB-DEPLOY initial design (SRE to confirm), not part of the 2026-11-18 decision (runbook section 1.6 item 6)
_offlineAcceptanceNotes.secrets: PLACEHOLDER ARNs - no plaintext DB/OIDC secrets in environment
_offlineAcceptanceNotes.requiredSettings: The canonical list of the settings prod refuses to start without is .kiro/specs/production-launch/deploy-runbook.md section 1.0 (rows 1-26 always; rows 27-30 only with FREEE_ENABLED=true); this template only carries their names. Every *_PLACEHOLDER value and ARN must be replaced; left unreplaced, the app or the task refuses to start. Key-version suffixes (_V1) must match the *_CURRENT_KEY_VERSION values. COMPLIANCE_GATE_FINGERPRINT_KEY_TENANTS lists the tenants whose fingerprint keys are read from the COMPLIANCE_GATE_FINGERPRINT_KEYS_<TENANT>_* variables. BREAK_GLASS_USERNAMES stays empty for the bootstrap start and gets exactly two names at runbook section 5.5. FREEE_ENABLED=false keeps freee off; to turn it on, set FREEE_ENABLED=true and add FREEE_CLIENT_ID, FREEE_CLIENT_SECRET, FREEE_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY (secrets) and FREEE_REDIRECT_URI (HTTPS), or the app refuses to start. TZ=Asia/Tokyo is required (runbook sections 1.0 and 4; the image also sets it and -Duser.timezone): without it the JVM runs in UTC, a 30-minute account lock lasts about 9.5 hours and timestamps shift by 9 hours. If you override JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, keep -Duser.timezone=Asia/Tokyo. RESUME_LEDGER_COPY_ALIGNMENT_ENABLED=false until the Privacy owner and document owner sign the V197 copy-disposal policy (runbook section 4.3); switch it to true after the signature.
_offlineAcceptanceNotes.initialStart: This template is the FIRST start (runbook sections 4 and 4.2): APP_SCHEDULING_ENABLED=false (one task, scheduler off; SchedulingConfig treats a missing value as true, so the scheduler would run without it), SECURITY_BOOTSTRAP_ENABLED=true, SECURITY_BOOTSTRAP_EXPIRES_AT replaced by an offset ISO-8601 time no more than 24 hours after the start (left unreplaced, the app refuses to start), BREAK_GLASS_USERNAMES empty, SECURITY_BOOTSTRAP_REOPEN_TICKET and LOCAL_LOGIN_ENABLED absent, and no feature switch variables. At runbook section 5.5 remove SECURITY_BOOTSTRAP_ENABLED and SECURITY_BOOTSTRAP_EXPIRES_AT and set BREAK_GLASS_USERNAMES to exactly two names. Set APP_SCHEDULING_ENABLED=true only after the sign-offs in runbook section 4.
_offlineAcceptanceNotes.FILE_SCANNER: Decided 2026-11-18 (runbook section 1.6 item 6): ClamAV (clamd INSTREAM) runs as a sidecar in this task and the task memory grows for it; so FILE_SCANNER_HOST=127.0.0.1 and FILE_SCANNER_PORT=3310 (the task shares one network namespace). Everything else about the sidecar is the RB-DEPLOY initial design that SRE confirms and measures: task 2048 CPU / 6144 MiB = app 1024 / 2048 (hard limit, so the JVM heap stays at 75% of 2048) + clamav 1024 / 4096; essential=false (the app keeps serving and uploads stay in quarantine while clamd is down; ECS does not restart a non-essential container, so detection and restart are SRE items); read-only root filesystem with the clamav-* bind volumes for the signature database, run, log and tmp; no secrets and no app settings in the sidecar; the image mirrored into ECR; clamdcheck.sh (the health script of the official image) as the health command. clamd should listen on 127.0.0.1 only (TCPAddr in clamd.conf of the mirrored image; SRE item). Uploads that arrived while clamd was down are not rescanned automatically; an administrator rescans them (runbook section 1.6 item 6).
_offlineAcceptanceNotes.METRICS_SCRAPER: Prometheus scrapes through the ALB over HTTPS with this machine account only (decided 2026-11-18, runbook section 1.6 item 7 and SRE-9), so METRICS_SCRAPER_ENABLED=true. METRICS_SCRAPER_USERNAME must not be admin or a break-glass name (always 401). METRICS_SCRAPER_PASSWORD comes from the secret store. The ALB listener rule / WAF restricts /actuator/prometheus to the scraper source.
_offlineAcceptanceNotes.PRIVACY_TRUST: Decided 2026-11-18 (runbook section 1.6 item 11): NF07 trust documents live on EFS, the app mounts them read only, and the D-03 owner updates the file. The RB-DEPLOY initial design: mount path /app/privacy-trust and an access point other than the uploads one. The read-only mount binds the app container only and is not an IAM boundary: ECS hands the task role credentials to every container in the task, the clamav sidecar included. Security confirms (runbook section 1.6 item 11): the EFS file system policy grants the task role ClientMount only on the privacy-trust access point and ClientWrite only on the uploads access point (condition elasticfilesystem:AccessPointArn), and the same policy lets the backup role write only through its one access point (uploads and backup staging under one root, so that both come from the same mount; the same POSIX user as the app, so the backup reads uploads read-only only through the :ro bind of its compose file, which Security accepts) and the restore principal write only the uploads access point; nobody writes through the privacy-trust read access point or the file system root, and only the D-03 owner role writes through the privacy-trust writer access point; the privacy-trust root is not contained in, and does not contain, the root of any other access point; both volumes mount with IAM authorization (iam ENABLED); the task role holds nothing else it does not need. PRIVACY_TRUST_KMS_ANCHOR_FILE stays empty for the first release (trust as in phase 1); when NF07 trust is opened, set it to the absolute path of the file under /app/privacy-trust/ (the NF07-TRUST section of the runbook).
_offlineAcceptanceNotes.BACKUP_QUIESCE: Backup write quiesce (RB-QUIESCE, deploy-runbook section 1.0 rows 31-41): BACKUP_QUIESCE_ENABLED=true is stated explicitly. false is the emergency stop (U-7) and starts only together with BACKUP_QUIESCE_DISABLED_TICKET in the change-ticket form ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$ (for example CHG-1234); while it is in effect every backup fails and the RPO alert fires. The other BACKUP_QUIESCE_* values are optional and must stay within the ranges of section 1.0 (written as <number><unit>, unit ms, s, m, h or d). healthCheck.startPeriod must be at least BACKUP_QUIESCE_STARTUP_WAIT_MAX (60s) + 120 seconds, and stopTimeout (120) at least SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT (30s) + 60 seconds (the task executor wait of 30 seconds and a margin for the 10-second drain before STOPPED). The DB_URL secret must not carry readOnlyPropagatesToServer=false: the app refuses to start.
_offlineAcceptanceNotes.validation: pwsh infra/ecs/offline/validate-task-definition.ps1 checks this template. Check the definition with real values with -Mode Actual -TaskDefinitionPath <file> (-Phase Initial for the first start; -Phase Steady -Scheduler Enabled|Disabled from runbook section 5.5); evidence goes outside the repository unless -EvidenceRoot says otherwise (runbook section 4). Remove this _offlineAcceptanceNotes block before registering: ECS rejects unknown fields and the Actual mode fails on it.
_offlineAcceptanceNotes.TRUSTED_PROXIES: PLACEHOLDER - replace with the ALB subnet CIDRs (comma separated; IPv4 must be RFC1918 or 100.64/10, /16 or narrower; IPv6 /48 or narrower). Left unreplaced, the app refuses to start (invalid CIDR). Never add 127.0.0.1: the container health check uses the plain-HTTP health path instead. See .kiro/specs/production-launch/forwarded-header-sanitize-notes.md

ecsContainerHealthCheck.note: Process liveness only; DB loss must not kill the task
ecsContainerHealthCheck.strictStatus: Healthy only on HTTP 200 (curl -w '%{http_code}' compared to 200). curl -f treats 302 as success, and no X-Forwarded-Proto is sent because a loopback peer is never trusted; /actuator/health{,/liveness,/readiness} answer over plain HTTP (FWD-SANITIZE P2-1)

efsUploads.accessPointRootPath: for example /ses-manager/files/uploads, under the root of the backup access point (runbook section 1.6 item 11 (b)(d)) - set on EFS Access Point (fsap-PLACEHOLDER), NOT in task efsVolumeConfiguration.rootDirectory when accessPointId is present
efsUploads.uploadBasePath: Decided 2026-11-18 (runbook section 1.6 item 11 (f), choice A): UPLOAD_BASE_PATH=/app/uploads/current, where current is a relative one-segment symlink in the uploads access point root that points to a version directory (current -> v0 at the first deployment). Create v0 and current through the uploads access point BEFORE the app starts for the first time: the app creates its subdirectories at startup, so a missing current would become a real directory and the pointer would be lost silently. A restore writes a new version directory and switches current with one rename while the app is stopped. The validator requires this exact value in both modes
efsUploads.taskRootDirectory: omit or "/" only when accessPointId is set (ECS API rule)

deferredExternalIac: EFS file system + access points (uploads, privacy-trust)
ECR repository for the ClamAV sidecar image
